html:
France is the state in western Europe that grew out of West Francia, the western share of the Frankish realm created by the Treaty of Verdun in 843. It has been a kingdom, an empire and a series of republics, and seeing it as one continuous state is partly hindsight.

The early kings were weak. In 987 the nobles chose Hugh Capet, whose family, the Capetians, ruled for centuries and slowly gathered land around Paris. Kings had to fight great vassals, above all the kings of England, who held large French lands. The Hundred Years' War (1337 to 1453) ended with the English pushed out, helped by Joan of Arc.

Main phases:

  • Wars of religion in the late 1500s, ended by Henry IV.
  • Absolute monarchy under Louis XIV (1643 to 1715), the strongest state in Europe.
  • The French Revolution from 1789, which ended the monarchy and spread ideas of rights and the nation.
  • Napoleon's empire and his Civil Code.
  • Restored kings, a second republic and empire, then the Third Republic from 1870.
  • Two world wars fought largely on or over its soil, defeat in 1940, and the Fifth Republic of Charles de Gaulle from 1958.

France built a large colonial empire in Africa, Asia and the Caribbean and gave up most of it after 1945. French was the language of European diplomacy and learning for two centuries, and Paris a world centre of art, from the Impressionists on. Since the 1950s France has been a founding member of what became the European Union.
